applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List (FTL)
assignment_rule: A traceability lot code must be assigned when: (1) initially packing a raw agricultural commodity other than a food obtained from a fishing vessel; (2) performing the first land-based receiving of a food obtained from a fishing vessel; or (3) transforming a food. No new TLC shall be established for other activities such as shipping.

citations.support_text: You must assign a traceability lot code when you do any of the following: Initially pack a raw agricultural commodity other than a food obtained from a fishing vessel; perform the first land-based receiving of a food obtained from a fishing vessel; or transform a food.

applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List received from a person to whom the subpart does not apply
assignment_rule: When receiving an FTL food from a person to whom the subpart does not apply, the receiver must assign a TLC if one has not already been assigned, except that this requirement does not apply to retail food establishments or restaurants.

applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List
preservation_rule: The existing traceability lot code must be preserved and carried through shipping and receiving events. No new TLC may be established solely because of a shipping or receiving activity. The shipper must provide the TLC to the immediate subsequent recipient.

applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List
source_reference_rule: For each traceability lot, records must include the location description for the traceability lot code source (i.e., the physical location where the TLC was assigned), and, if applicable, the traceability lot code source reference. This applies at shipping, receiving, initial packing, first land-based receiving, and transformation CTEs.

applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List produced through transformation
transformation_handling: When a food is produced through transformation, a new traceability lot code must be assigned to the output lot. Records must link the new TLC to: (1) the TLC(s) of each FTL input food used, including product description and quantity used from each input lot; (2) the new TLC for the output food; (3) the location where transformation occurred (TLC source) and, if applicable, the TLC source reference; (4) the date transformation was completed; (5) the product description and quantity of the output food; and (6) the reference document type and number.
lineage_rule: Each new traceability lot produced through transformation must be linked to the traceability lot codes of all FTL foods used as inputs in that transformation event.

applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List
lineage_rule: At shipping, the shipper must provide the TLC, product description, quantity, location of immediate subsequent recipient, shipping location, shipping date, and TLC source or TLC source reference to the immediate subsequent recipient in electronic, paper, or other written form. At receiving, the receiver must maintain records linking the TLC to the immediate previous source, receiving location, receipt date, and TLC source or TLC source reference.

applies_to_food_scope: Foods on the Food Traceability List
uniqueness_rule: A traceability lot code must meet the regulatory definition of 'traceability lot code.' Industry best practices support using a combination of a globally unique product identifier, firm-assigned internal lot code, and standard date code to uniquely identify a lot. Examples include Julian date, lot code, batch code, or other production code, provided the combination meets the regulatory definition.

citations.citation_anchor: What are some examples of traceability lot codes?
citations.section_ref: What are some examples of traceability lot codes?
citations.support_text: Several food industry-supported traceability initiatives offer best practices and standards for uniquely identifying a lot of food using a combination of a globally unique product identifier, firm-assigned internal lot code, and standard date code. Other examples include a Julian date, a lot code, batch code or other production code. This information, taken together, could be used as a traceability lot code, provided it meets the definition of “traceability lot code” in the final rule.

reviewer_notes: The uniqueness requirement is implied by the regulatory definition of 'traceability lot code' referenced in the FDA guidance but the definition text itself is not present in the supplied source chunks. Reviewer should confirm against the full regulatory definition at 21 CFR 1.1310.

applies_to_food_scope: Food obtained from a fishing vessel for which the entity is the first land-based receiver
source_reference_rule: For each traceability lot of food obtained from a fishing vessel, the first land-based receiver must record the location description for the first land-based receiver as the TLC source, and, if applicable, the TLC source reference. Records must also include harvest date range and locations identified under NMFS Ocean Geographic Code, FAO Major Fishing Area list, or any other widely recognized geographical location standard.
